bluf: Hawke Media is a Santa Monica performance agency that sells itself as an outsourced CMO for growth stage brands, every service a la carte, backed by an in house platform it calls Hawke AI. It is pushing AI search: a GEO and AEO offer launched in 2025-12 with AI answer audits, content and schema strategy, and its Google and LinkedIn ads now sell SEO paired with GEO. What a rival should know: the record names not one client, its sitemap shows 0 URLs updated in 90 days, and the AI offer has no audited visibility product behind it.
doing:
The positioning line reads: outsourced CMO for growth stage brands, a full service performance agency selling a la carte services from strategy and media to lifecycle, backed by Hawke AI. In plain words, a menu of channel services for smaller brands with a platform label on top and a registered engagement mark, Your Outsourced CMO. The headline claim of 5,000+ brands grown across more than 70 categories has no named client anywhere in the record to test it.

Service lines run from Strategy, Paid Search, Paid Social and SEO through GEO and AEO, Lifecycle Marketing, Amazon Services, Connected TV and Media Buying to Affiliate Marketing, Public Relations and Web Design; Hawke AI is the proprietary platform and Birdeye the one partner. No line leads: five core lines all score 2. AI Search rests on a GEO and AEO page with an AI footprint audit; Email & CRM on lifecycle email and SMS pitched on revenue and retention; Paid Search on 103 of its own Google ads, 17 in 30 days; Paid Social on paid social, TikTok Shop and social media pages; SEO on a service page and 799 insight posts. Seven lines score 1; B2B, CRO and Data & Measurement score 0.

Its AI posture is the 2025-12 launch of AI answer audits, content and schema strategy, plus the Hawke AI platform credited across delivery: a service line and a production claim, no audited visibility product, no agent line. That 2025-12 announcement of an AI powered search optimization offering is the one dated move. Pricing signals: everything a la carte, ads and nav pushing a free marketing consultation, no public pricing model. Absent for an agency claiming 5,000+ brands: a single case study, client name, vertical, job, news item, office, owner, founding year or employee count; the about page tallies awards instead, 12 Stevie, 5 Inc. 5000, 9 dotComm, 5 Globee and 2 Adweek.
clients:
The client type is mixed, and the positioning says growth stage brands. The record lists no vertical and no client: the needs read holds 0 clients, 0 observed and 0 named only, with no evidence type, no mix and an empty shared list, so nothing on this book can be matched against another tracked agency. The home market is the US from Santa Monica, with no other office listed.

The only statement about clients in the record is the headline claim of 5,000+ brands across more than 70 categories, and it names none. What the book came for cannot be observed; it can only be inferred from the sold mix, and the sentence says so. That mix points at ecommerce brands: Amazon Services, a TikTok Shop page, lifecycle email and SMS pitched on revenue and retention, affiliate marketing and Connected TV are the services of a shop serving brands that sell online. The Birdeye service line adds a reputation offer, which reads as local and lead generation for a different buyer, inferred from the partner listing alone.

What the base needs next, as a judgment: the mix is best placed for KJ1, the click is being replaced by the citation, and most exposed to KJ6, the agency middle is being hollowed out, on paid search, paid social and SEO hours. It is likely, low confidence since no client is named, that growth stage brands buying a la carte channels next ask for the measurement the record does not sell (Data & Measurement scores 0) and for an audited AI visibility number behind the GEO offer, which P1 partial says it does not yet show; roughly even chance the a la carte menu itself is the retention risk under KJ6.
house:
Say and do: four lines tested, all four practised, integrity 100. Paid Search is corroborated: 107 Google ads of its own, 17 in the last 30 days, 90 text, 11 image and 6 video, last shown 2026-09-27; one sample reads: Book a Free Consultation, Gen AI SEO, GEO for Your Business. Paid Social is corroborated by TikTok and X pixels on its own site. LinkedIn advertising is corroborated: 20 company page ads, one reading: The future of search isn't SEO versus GEO. It's both. Publishing cadence passes the test, though the sitemap lists 852 URLs with 0 updated in 90 days and 47 in 365. AI Search is unknown because the llms.txt check did not complete. No gap is flagged, no AI crawler blocked.

The stack is GTM, GA4, Microsoft UET, HubSpot, Hotjar and the TikTok and X pixels on WordPress with Elementor; no test tool and no ABM stack. Meta and TikTok libraries: the record is silent.
market:
Horus reads 3.6, Neutral. Best placed for KJ1, the click is being replaced by the citation (net 0.257, AI Search / GEO), and KJ2, ads inside AI answers (net 0.206). Most exposed to KJ6, the agency middle is being hollowed out (net minus 0.199, Paid Search, Paid Social and SEO), and KJ4, the platforms are absorbing the execution layer (net minus 0.154, Paid Search and Paid Social at minus 2 each). The mix sits at 16:19 on the Solar Arc; best fit is The Walled Oasis at 35/100. It is making P2 (schema work beside a core SEO line), partial on P1 (audited AI visibility), P4 (no first party data or measurement depth) and P7, absent on P3, P6 and P8, unknown on P5.

Monsoon reads 54.4, Breeze: migration 52.9 against displacement 55.9, SEO (11) and Paid Search (7) carrying the most movable hours, automation overlapping 22%. Shore: 65% South and Southeast Asia, 25% Latin America. The footprint is inferred, no hub office listed; the onshore claim in its own words is the in house Hawke AI platform.
openings:
The strongest opening is the empty book: an agency claiming 5,000+ brands names none in its record, so a rival with named, described work in the same growth stage ecommerce space is likely, moderate confidence, to win any pitch where proof is asked for. Falsifier: named client case studies appearing on hawkemedia.com.

Second, AI: it sells GEO and AEO with AI answer audits, yet P1 is partial with no audited citation share, so a rival leading with the audited number is likely to take that conversation, moderate confidence. Third, measurement: Data & Measurement scores 0, P4 is partial, and KJ6 and KJ4 both press on its paid hours, so an offer led by first party data and measurement depth undercuts the data driven claim in its own ads. Fourth, no public pricing (P5 unknown) beneath an a la carte menu invites an outcome priced bundle. Fifth, cadence: 0 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days against 799 insight posts, a content engine that has stopped. Price is a weak lever: Monsoon reads Breeze at 54.4 and it claims onshore delivery through Hawke AI, so an offshore undercut is unlikely to bite beyond the SEO and paid search hours.
